claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives with me at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can see you have a son named Alex who is 17 and lives with you at home.

Since Alex is 17, I need to ask: **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (This could include things like A-levels, Scottish Highers, NVQs, or other approved courses.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He left school and isn't studying anything right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. I need to ask: **Is Alex working, and if so, how many hours per week does he work?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment. He's just at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. One more important question: **Has Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?** 

(If he left education or training recently and registered with one of these, you may still be able to claim Child Benefit for up to 20 weeks.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with anything like that. He just finished school and hasn't signed up with any careers service or anything.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I also need to check a couple more things:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

**How long ago did Alex leave education?** (For example, did he leave recently or has it been several months?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It's been a few months now since he left school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- While you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, the rules are different for older children
- For 16 and 17 year olds like Alex, Child Benefit can only continue if they are in **approved education or training**
- Since Alex left school a few months ago and is not currently in any education or training, this condition is not met
- There is a potential 20-week extension if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, but Alex has not done this
- Even if he were to register now, since he left school several months ago, the 20-week period would likely have already passed

**What you could consider:**
- If Alex enrolls in approved education or training (such as college courses, A-levels, or vocational training), you could become eligible again
- If Alex registers with a careers service soon after leaving education, this might help with future eligibility, though the 20-week period from when he left school may have already expired

I hope this explanation is helpful. Please let me know if you have any other questions.

Since Alex is not in approved education or training and has not registered with a careers service or armed services, and it has been several months since he left school, the claimant is not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.
